reported.title: E-stop logic inverted: contactor energized while e-stop pressed
reported.description: estopActive() at lines 18-21 returns true when the pin reads HIGH, but the e-stop is active LOW (pressed = LOW), so the polarity is backwards. With D3 held LOW the code treats the e-stop as clear and drives D5 HIGH (lines 76-83), and with D3 HIGH it treats it as pressed and drives D5 LOW, matching the measured 'D5 was not HIGH for 900 ms while required' and 'D5 was not LOW for 900 ms while required' intervals. The trip counter at lines 62-65 also increments on release rather than press for the same reason. D5 was in the wrong state for 4842 ms across 31 interval(s), first at 100 ms: D5 was not HIGH for 700 ms while required (grace 100 ms).

truth.description: E-stop polarity inverted vs pull-up wiring

exposing_checks.behaviour: D5 must follow its stimulus; HIGH when D3 == 1; LOW when D3 == 0; within 100 ms (Contactor follows e-stop)

judge_input.spec:
- E-stop on D3 with INPUT_PULLUP, active LOW when pressed. Contactor coil on D5. Run request on D6 (pull-up).
- Contactor D5 must drop LOW when e-stop is held (D3 LOW), and run HIGH when e-stop is released.
- React within 100 ms of a settled e-stop level change.
- Settle the e-stop contact for 30 ms before counting a new trip.
- Print `hoist run=<0|1> trips=<n>` every 1100 ms.
- When e-stop is clear, keep the contactor available (HIGH) for hoist motion.
